propositions: A deterministic AST gate must detect six categories of prohibited env/config reads below approved seam boundaries: ambient env read, helper-shim env read, load_config call, literal-getattr env equivalent, provider-credential read, and configurable adapter default/backend reload.

The gate must reuse gen_env_registry.py's scan, KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS, and matchers (direct import, single source) and add receiver-object aliasing resolution so that indirect reads like `src = os.environ; src.get('SECRET')` are detected.

The approved-seam registry must enumerate composition roots (config.py, _config_sources.py, _child_env.py, model adapters) and provider-credential boundaries (four specific rebar_reconciler modules), derive owner sets from existing registries (_child_env.owned_secret_names, @register decorators from adapters/), and reject path-glob exceptions structurally.
Unresolved env reads (shim-shaped calls absent from KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS, dynamic env-name args) must fail closed and be reported as unresolved-env-read violations.

A legacy-exception set enumerates current below-seam reads so the gate is introducible without product-code changes; newly declared env names or credential names without an owner must cause the gate to fail (drift self-test).

The gate must expose check(root)->list[str] and main(argv)->int contracts, run offline with no network/CI dependency, exit 0 on the current tree, and include synthetic fixtures for all six categories and edge cases (import-aliased, local-aliased, receiver-aliased forms).
